findings.title: Traceability with a focused record: the note 'Showing the links of <type> "<name>"' (TraceabilityPage.tsx, p.small[data-root]) prints the record name as plain text outside .record-name, so an unbroken record name still widens the page (651 px at 390 px, 721 px at 320 px, 1312 px at 200 % with a 120-character word; 85-155 px with an unbroken Arabic token), in en and ar
findings.reproduction: Disposable complete clone of the frozen candidate (1932faa = source 12dc33e + delivery records; sha256:33188e9e...), offline install, pnpm -r build, production-initialized stack. Copy docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/qa/tests/round-7/e2e/zz-qa-dg5r7-trace-root-note.spec.ts into the clone's e2e/ and run 'E2E_PG_PORT=26612 E2E_API_PORT=26613 apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh npx playwright test <clone>/e2e/zz-qa-dg5r7-trace-root-note.spec.ts --workers=1' (PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers), with the locale unset and with LANG=LC_ALL=C.UTF-8. As dev.lead, per language and token (w120: 'Synthetic_' + 110 letters with no break opportunity; arU: an unbroken 69-character Arabic token joined by underscores; plain: ordinary text) it creates a SYNTHETIC transformation with one Define outcome holding the token, opens /transformations/<T>/traceability at 390, 360 and 320 px, measures document.documentElement.scrollWidth - innerWidth, then clicks the outcome node's 'Focus' button (data-action='focus', which sets ?root=) and measures again (R7-TRACE-FOCUS-CLICK). R7-TRACE-ROOT opens the same state by URL and, as a diagnosis only, sets overflow-wrap:anywhere on the [data-root] note through the CSSOM in the page (never in the product) to show that the note is the only cause. The asserted probe R7-F148 (zz-qa-dg5r7-f148-f149-verify.spec.ts) shows the same values for the Traceability state with ?root=&impact=&alloc=.
findings.expected: No page-level horizontal scroll whatever text a user enters in a record name, on every state of the Traceability screen (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.10 Reflow; the rule wave AB applied to RecordName and the Modular entry label as .record-name, overflow-wrap: anywhere).
findings.actual:
Identical in en and ar and in both locale settings (4 runs). Before the click: 0 px for every token. After clicking Focus: w120 651 px at 390, 681 px at 360, 721 px at 320 (the note's own scrollWidth - clientWidth 680/710/750 px); arU 85/115/155 px; the 46-character token 40 px at 320 px; plain 0 px. With 200 % text at 1280 px: w120 1312 px, arU 210 px. With the diagnostic style on the note only, every case is 0 px, so the note is the sole cause. In the screenshot (en, arU, 390 px) the graph's record link wraps (the wave AB fix works) while the note's text runs past the right edge. Cause in source: TraceabilityPage.tsx renders t('traceability.graph.rooted', {type, name}) in

, and the record name is interpolated as plain text, not through RecordName/.record-name; wave AB (T-DG5-FE-AB1) did not touch this element, and my round-6 reproduction (which this round re-runs unchanged: 0 px everywhere) never focused a record, so F-DG5-148 did not name it. Not a regression of the repair: the note is a DG4 element that ad52a56..12dc33e leaves unchanged. It needs an unusual name and REQ-S15-009 is DG6-final, so it is Low, not mandatory and not blocking DG5. Suggested fix: render the name in the note with the same .record-name rule (or overflow-wrap:anywhere on [data-root]), and extend p5-record-name-reflow.spec.ts to click Focus.

findings.title: The product e2e test p5-launch-health-kpi.spec.ts:159 (the test D-182 saw fail once) synchronizes on 'any GET of the assessment' after Save actions; with a slow API that wait resolves on the GET issued by the earlier refused Submit's refresh (the pre-save version), so the test can click Submit before the screen holds the saved version: an unsound wait, and a plausible but unproven cause of the D-182 failure
findings.reproduction: Disposable complete clone of the frozen candidate (sha256:33188e9e..., source 12dc33e), production-initialized stack. Copy docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/qa/tests/round-7/e2e/zz-qa-dg5r7-health-submit-race.spec.ts into the clone's e2e/ and run 'QA_SLOW_MS=1500 E2E_PG_PORT=26622 E2E_API_PORT=26623 apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh npx playwright test <clone>/e2e/zz-qa-dg5r7-health-submit-race.spec.ts --grep R7-HEALTH-SLOWGET --repeat-each=3 --workers=1' (and QA_SLOW_MS=0 as the control). R7-HEALTH-SLOWGET replays the product test's ending with the product test's own waits (saved = the PUT .../actions response; reloaded = the first GET .../health-checks/<id> response after the waiter is registered; then Submit and the 5 s 'submitted' assertion), and answers every GET of the assessment after QA_SLOW_MS (route.fetch, pause, fulfil: a slow server). It records which GET resolved 'reloaded' (numbered by a test-only header), its version, the If-Match the screen sent and the outcome.
findings.expected: The test waits for a signal that the saved version is on the screen (for example the response of a GET issued after the PUT response, or a rendered marker of the new version) before it clicks Submit, so the test cannot fail because of response ordering under load.
findings.actual: QA_SLOW_MS=1500, 6/6 runs (en and ar): 'reloaded' resolved with GET #1, issued at about 147 ms, BEFORE the Save-actions click at about 275 ms (the refresh that useRunner starts after the refused Submit; automation/ui.tsx shows the alert before 'await refresh()'), carrying version 26, while the PUT had produced version 27. The product nevertheless sent If-Match "27" and showed 'submitted' within 5 s in every run, because the click landed after the post-save GET #2 had returned (about 1880 ms vs 2000 ms). So the race window exists in the test, while the product behaved correctly in every run. A stale If-Match would be answered 409, the correct optimistic-concurrency result, and the test would then fail. QA_SLOW_MS=0 control: 6/6, 'reloaded' = the post-save GET. Not reproduced otherwise: the product test passed in all 4 full product runs (460/460 with the locale unset and with C.UTF-8), 10/10 alone in chromium-ar (--repeat-each=10, beside the C.UTF-8 product run), and R7-HEALTH-RACE 5/5 at CPU rate 1 and 5/5 at rate 4 (If-Match = the saved version every time, submitted shown in 166-559 ms). The D-182 trace is lost, so its cause stays unestablished. I find no evidence of a product defect: the screen always sent the current version and the server accepted it. The test defect is demonstrated. Low, not mandatory, not blocking DG5.
